generated.title: M6.2 Earthquake Strikes Deep Beneath Vanuatu | Next Huge Quake #shorts
generated.description:
A magnitude 6.2 earthquake struck deep beneath Vanuatu on October 29, 2026 at 21:46 UTC (08:46 on October 30, local time), about 43 km east-southeast of Port-Olry, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS).

What USGS reports:
- Magnitude: M6.2 (Mww); the event data has been reviewed by USGS
- Depth: about 143 km (142.8 km), an intermediate-depth earthquake
- Epicenter: 15.19°S, 167.45°E, offshore east of Espiritu Santo
- PAGER alert: green, the lowest level. PAGER is a modeled estimate of potential fatalities and economic losses, not a report of what actually happened
- ShakeMap: strongest estimated shaking intensity IV (light)
- Did You Feel It?: 2 reports as of the USGS update at 22:40 UTC (a count of submitted reports, not of people)
- Tsunami: the USGS record carries no tsunami flag for this earthquake

Why so deep? Vanuatu sits above the New Hebrides subduction zone, where the Australian plate descends beneath the Pacific plate. Earthquakes at this depth typically occur inside the descending plate. Deeper earthquakes generally produce less intense shaking at the surface than shallow ones of the same magnitude.

In the information we reviewed, no damage or casualties have been reported. This may change as more information becomes available. Magnitudes are USGS values and may be revised; other agencies can publish different preliminary values.

Official event page: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us7000tu4f

Narration is an AI-generated voice (ElevenLabs text-to-speech). The video contains no AI-generated images or footage; the map is drawn from USGS data, Natural Earth and Mapzen terrain.
